definition: A response delivery mode where a language model's output is sent incrementally, token by token or in small chunks, as it's generated, rather than waiting for the complete response.
details: Streaming significantly improves perceived responsiveness in interactive applications like chat interfaces, allowing users to start reading a response before the model has finished generating it entirely.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Streaming (in LLM APIs) — is what makes everything else possible.
